topics.title: Gotchas
topics.content_html:
# Mutable default — shared across calls
def append(item, bucket=[]):   # BAD
    bucket.append(item); return bucket

def append(item, bucket=None):  # GOOD
    if bucket is None: bucket = []
    bucket.append(item); return bucket

# is vs ==
a is b          # identity
a == b          # equality

# Late-binding closures
funcs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
funcs[0]()      # 2 — all see final i
funcs = [lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)]  # capture

# Generator exhaustion
g = (x*x for x in range(3))
list(g); list(g)  # second is []

# Prefer specific exceptions over bare except
Common mistake Mutable defaults and late-binding closures are classic traps. Prefer None defaults and default-arg capture in lambdas.

topics.title: Ownership & Borrowing
topics.content_html:
Every value has one owner. Non-Copy assignment moves; the old binding is invalid.

let s1 = String::from("hello");
let s2 = s1;                  // move — s1 invalid
println!("{s2}");

let n1 = 5;                   // i32 is Copy
let n2 = n1;                  // both valid

fn print_len(s: &String) -> usize { s.len() }
print_len(&s);                // borrow, s still valid

fn add_world(s: &mut String) { s.push_str(", world"); }
let mut s = String::from("hello");
add_world(&mut s);

// either one &mut OR any number of & — never both
let s3 = s2.clone();
★ Ownership defaults Prefer borrowing (&T / &mut T) over cloning. Own with T only when you need exclusive ownership.
Need ownership? │ ├─ no -> borrow │ ├─ read-only -> &T │ └─ mutate -> &mut T └─ yes -> move T └─ shared ownership? -> Arc<T> (or Rc<T> single-threaded)
Common mistake Don't clone() just to silence the borrow checker — prefer a borrow or a redesign.

topics.title: Error Handling
topics.content_html:
No exceptions. Recoverable: Result<T, E>. Unrecoverable: panic!.

fn divide(a: f64, b: f64) -> Result<f64, String> {
    if b == 0.0 { return Err("Cannot divide by zero!".into()); }
    Ok(a / b)
}

match divide(10.0, 0.0) {
    Ok(r) => println!("Result: {r}"),
    Err(e) => println!("{e}"),
}

fn read_number() -> Result<i32, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string("num.txt")?;
    let n: i32 = s.trim().parse()?;
    Ok(n)
}

result.unwrap_or(0);

topics.title: Gotchas
topics.content_html:
// Unnecessary clone — prefer a borrow
let s2 = s1.clone();   // only when you need ownership

// Borrowing across mutation
let r = &v[0];
v.push(1);             // error while r lives

// unwrap in libraries
value.unwrap();        // prefer ? / unwrap_or / ok_or

// Blocking inside async
std::thread::sleep(...);  // use tokio::time::sleep

// Mutex poisoning — a panic while holding the lock poisons it;
// later .lock() calls return Err instead of panicking silently
let guard = match mutex.lock() {
    Ok(g) => g,
    Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner(), // recover the data anyway
};

// Prefer &T / &mut T; Arc only for shared ownership across threads
Common mistake clone() and unwrap() silence the compiler but hide design issues. Prefer borrows and ? propagation.

function* range(start, end) {
  for (let i = start; i < end; i++) yield i;
}
[...range(0, 3)];                 // [0, 1, 2]

class Countdown {
  constructor(from) { this.from = from; }
  *[Symbol.iterator]() {
    for (let i = this.from; i > 0; i--) yield i;
  }
}
[...new Countdown(3)];            // [3, 2, 1]

const it = [10, 20][Symbol.iterator]();
it.next();                        // { value: 10, done: false }

// Iterator helpers (ES2025): lazy, one value at a time
range(0, Infinity)
  .filter((n) => n % 2 === 0)
  .map((n) => n * n)
  .take(3)
  .toArray();                     // [0, 4, 16]

// Async iteration
for await (const chunk of stream) {}
★ Default Use a generator function to make a custom sequence. It already implements the iterator protocol.
Common mistake An iterator can only be consumed once. Spreading a generator twice gives an empty second result.
topics.search_keywords: iterator iterable generator yield for of symbol iterator async iteration iterator helpers take map filter

topics.title: Regular Expressions
topics.content_html:
const re = /(?<year>\d{4})-(?<month>\d{2})/u;
const match = "Released 2026-06".match(re);
match.groups.year;                        // "2026"

"a1b2".replace(/\d/g, (d) => d * 2);      // "a2b4"
"2026-06".replace(re, "$<month>/$<year>");  // "06/2026"

for (const m of "one two".matchAll(/\w+/g)) {
  console.log(m[0], m.index);
}

/(?<=\$)\d+/.exec("cost $42")[0];         // "42" (lookbehind)
/\p{L}+/u.test("héllo");                  // true (Unicode property)

new RegExp(RegExp.escape(userInput), "i");   // safe pattern from text
FlagMeaning
gfind every match
iignore case
m^ and $ match at line breaks
s. also matches newlines
u / vUnicode mode; v adds set operations
ysticky: match only at lastIndex
dreport match start and end indices
★ Default Add the u flag (or v) so patterns treat text as Unicode code points.
Common mistake A regular expression with the g flag remembers lastIndex, so calling test() on it repeatedly can alternate between true and false. Create it inside the function, or reset lastIndex.

topics.title: JSON
topics.content_html:
const text = JSON.stringify({ id: 1, tags: ["a", "b"] }, null, 2);   // pretty-printed
const data = JSON.parse(text);

// Reviver: rebuild values while parsing
const parsed = JSON.parse('{"when":"2026-06-30T00:00:00.000Z"}', (key, value) =>
  key === "when" ? new Date(value) : value
);

// What stringify leaves out or changes
JSON.stringify({ a: undefined, b: () => 1, c: NaN });   // '{"c":null}'
JSON.stringify(new Date(0));                            // '"1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"'
// JSON.stringify(10n);                                  // TypeError: BigInt

// Control the output with toJSON
const money = { cents: 250, toJSON() { return (this.cents / 100).toFixed(2); } };
JSON.stringify(money);                                   // '"2.50"'

try {
  JSON.parse("{ invalid }");
} catch (error) {
  console.log(error instanceof SyntaxError);             // true
}
★ Default Always wrap JSON.parse() of outside input in try/catch; invalid text throws a SyntaxError.
Common mistake undefined, functions and symbols are dropped from objects, NaN becomes null, and BigInt throws. Dates come back as strings, so convert them with a reviver.

topics.title: Dates & Time
topics.content_html:
const now = new Date();
Date.now();                                   // milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC
new Date("2026-06-30T12:00:00Z").toISOString();
new Date(2026, 5, 30);                        // month is 0-based: this is June

const d = new Date("2026-06-30T12:00:00Z");
d.getUTCFullYear();                           // 2026
d.getTime();                                  // number of milliseconds
d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + 7);             // adds a week, and mutates d

new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { dateStyle: "medium", timeZone: "UTC" }).format(d);
d.toLocaleDateString("en-US", { month: "long", day: "numeric" });

// Temporal: the modern API (ES2027 draft, check runtime support first)
const today = Temporal.Now.plainDateISO();
Temporal.PlainDate.from("2026-06-30").add({ days: 7 });
★ Default Store and send time as UTC ISO strings, and format it for people with Intl.DateTimeFormat.
Common mistake new Date(2026, 5, 30) is June, because months start at 0. A date-only string like "2026-06-30" is read as UTC, while "2026-06-30T00:00:00" is read as local time.

topics.title: Async & Await
topics.content_html:
async function load(url) {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(url);      // fetch is a host API
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
    return await response.json();
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("load failed", error);
    throw error;
  }
}

const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Parallel instead of one after another
const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([load("/users"), load("/posts")]);

await Promise.allSettled(tasks);       // every outcome, never rejects
await Promise.race([task(), sleep(1000)]);
await Promise.any([mirrorA(), mirrorB()]);   // first success

const { promise, resolve, reject } = Promise.withResolvers();

const controller = new AbortController();  // host API for cancelling
fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal });
controller.abort();
★ Default Start independent work together and await the group with Promise.all(), instead of awaiting one call after another.
Common mistake array.forEach(async ...) does not wait for the promises it creates. Use for...of with await, or Promise.all(array.map(...)). A promise that rejects with nobody handling it is reported as an unhandled rejection.
topics.search_keywords: async await promise all allSettled race any withResolvers try setTimeout abort fetch sequential parallel

topics.title: Modules
topics.content_html:
// math.js
export const PI = 3.14159;
export function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
export default class Calculator {}
// main.js
import Calculator, { PI, add as sum } from "./math.js";
import * as math from "./math.js";
import data from "./data.json" with { type: "json" };

export * from "./helpers.js";
export * as utils from "./utils.js";

const heavy = await import("./heavy.js");   // dynamic import, top-level await
console.log(import.meta.url);               // location of this module
// CommonJS, the older Node.js style
const fs = require("fs");
module.exports = { read: (path) => fs.readFileSync(path, "utf8") };
★ Default Use ES modules with explicit file extensions in import paths.
Common mistake import and require do not mix freely. Node.js treats .mjs files, and .js files under "type": "module" in package.json, as modules. In a browser use <script type="module">.
topics.search_keywords: module import export default dynamic import require commonjs esm import.meta top-level await json type module

topics.title: Errors
topics.content_html:
try {
  risky();
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TypeError) {
    recover();
  } else {
    throw error;                  // do not swallow what you cannot handle
  }
} finally {
  cleanup();                      // always runs
}

class ValidationError extends Error {
  constructor(message, options) {
    super(message, options);
    this.name = "ValidationError";
  }
}

try {
  parse(input);
} catch (cause) {
  throw new ValidationError("Invalid input", { cause });   // keep the original error
}

Error.isError(value);             // true for real errors, even from another realm
new AggregateError([new Error("a"), new Error("b")], "several failed");
★ Default Throw Error objects, not strings, so callers get a stack trace and a name.
Common mistake catch (error) can receive anything that was thrown, so check its type before using error.message. Optional catch binding, catch { }, is fine when the error is not needed.
topics.search_keywords: error try catch finally throw custom error cause aggregate rangeerror typeerror isError

topics.title: Gotchas
topics.content_html:
0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3;             // false
"10" + 1;                      // "101"  (string concatenation)
"10" - 1;                      // 9      (numeric subtraction)
[] + {};                       // "[object Object]"

parseInt("12px");              // 12
Number("12px");                // NaN
[1, 2, 3].map(parseInt);       // [1, NaN, NaN]  (index is passed as the radix)
typeof NaN;                    // "number"
NaN === NaN;                   // false

Array(3).fill([]);             // three references to the SAME array
const grid = Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => []);   // three separate arrays

const arr = [1, 2, 3];
delete arr[1];                 // leaves a hole: [1, empty, 3]
arr.length;                    // still 3

[10, 2, 1].sort();             // [1, 10, 2]
Common mistake Most of these come from implicit type coercion. Convert values explicitly with Number(), String() and Boolean(), and compare with ===.

site.home_meta_description: An extensible syntax reference for switching between languages.
site.home_description: A practical reference for anyone who works with multiple programming languages. Quickly find familiar syntax, concepts, patterns, and common gotchas — no matter which language you are working in.
site.footer: Polyglot Syntax Reference · Open source · For every programmer
site.compare_description: Side-by-side syntax comparison across the supported languages.
site.compare_intro: Jump between the supported languages without losing your place.

versions.label: ES3 (baseline)
versions.note: Baseline. Features that have existed since the earliest editions (ES1 to ES3) are recorded as added here.

versions.label: ES2027
versions.note: Draft edition, expected June 2027. Contents can still change.

features.title: with statement
features.summary: Adds an object's properties to the scope chain for a block, so bare names resolve against the object.

history.note: Using with in strict-mode code is a SyntaxError. Sloppy-mode code can still use it, but class bodies and modules are always strict.

migration.modern:
const { host, port } = config.server;
console.log(host, port);
migration.note: Destructure the names you need into local constants (ES2015).

features.title: arguments.callee
features.summary: arguments.callee refers to the function that is currently running, from inside that function.

history.note: Accessing arguments.callee throws a TypeError in strict-mode functions.

migration.note: Give the function expression a name and call it by that name.

features.title: Legacy octal literals
features.summary: Integer literals written with a leading zero, such as 0755, and octal escape sequences in strings.

history.note: Described in the compatibility annex (Annex B) rather than the core grammar.
Legacy octal literals and octal escape sequences are a SyntaxError in strict mode.

migration.note: Use the 0o prefix (ES2015).

features.title: String.prototype.substr()
features.summary: Extracts part of a string using a start index and a length.

history.note: New in the compatibility annex (Annex B), which first appeared in ES3. Not part of the core language.
Legacy feature kept for web compatibility (Annex B). Prefer slice() or substring(). It is not scheduled for removal.

migration.note: substr takes (start, length); slice takes (start, end).

features.title: escape() and unescape()
features.summary: Global functions that apply a percent-style encoding to strings.

history.note: Part of the core language in the earliest editions. Moved to the compatibility annex (Annex B) in ES3.
Legacy functions kept for web compatibility (Annex B). They use a non-standard %uXXXX form for characters above U+00FF. Use encodeURIComponent() and decodeURIComponent().

migration.note: Results differ for non-ASCII characters and for characters such as +, / and @.

features.title: encodeURI() and encodeURIComponent()
features.summary: Functions that encode and decode strings for use inside URIs.

features.title: for...in enumeration
features.summary: for...in loops over an object's enumerable string keys, including inherited ones.

history.note: The order is now partly specified. For ordinary objects, own keys come first (integer indices in ascending order, then string keys in the order they were added), followed by inherited keys. Proxies and other exotic objects, and objects changed during the loop, can still differ.

features.title: Strict mode
features.summary: The 'use strict' directive switches code to a restricted variant of the language with more errors.

history.note: Class bodies and module code are always strict, with no directive needed.

features.title: JSON.parse() and JSON.stringify()
features.summary: A built-in JSON object for parsing and producing JSON text.

history.note: JSON.stringify now escapes lone surrogates so its output is always well-formed, and U+2028 and U+2029 are allowed inside string literals.

migration.note: eval runs arbitrary code; JSON.parse only parses data.

features.title: Array iteration methods
features.summary: forEach, map, filter, reduce, reduceRight, some, every, indexOf and lastIndexOf on arrays.

features.title: Function.prototype.bind()
features.summary: Returns a function with a fixed this value and optional leading arguments.

features.title: let and const
features.summary: Block-scoped variable declarations, with const for bindings that are never reassigned.

migration.note: var is function-scoped, so every callback sees the final i (3). let creates a new binding per iteration (0, 1, 2).

features.title: Arrow functions
features.summary: Compact function syntax whose this is taken from the surrounding code.

migration.note: Arrow functions have no own this, arguments or prototype, so they cannot replace every function expression.

features.title: Classes
features.summary: class declarations with constructors, methods, extends and super.

history.note: Class bodies gained public and private fields, private methods and static initialization blocks.

migration.note: A class must be called with new, and class declarations are not usable before their line runs.

features.title: Template literals
features.summary: Backtick strings with ${expression} interpolation, multi-line text and tagged templates.

history.note: Tagged templates may contain invalid escape sequences; their cooked value is undefined instead of a SyntaxError.

migration.legacy: var message = "Hello, " + name + "! You have " + count + " messages.";

features.title: Destructuring
features.summary: Pattern syntax that unpacks arrays and objects into variables.

migration.legacy:
var host = options.host;
var port = options.port;

features.title: Default, rest and spread parameters
features.summary: Default parameter values, rest parameters, and spread in calls and array literals.

migration.note: A default applies only when the argument is undefined. The || pattern also replaces 0, empty strings and false.

features.title: ES modules
features.summary: import and export statements for native modules.

features.title: Promises
features.summary: Promise objects for asynchronous results, with then, catch, Promise.all and Promise.race.

migration.note: The functions must return promises. Wrap callback-style APIs with new Promise.

features.title: Binary and octal literals
features.summary: 0b and 0o prefixes for binary and octal integer literals.

features.title: includes(), startsWith(), endsWith() and repeat()
features.summary: String methods for testing whether text contains, starts with or ends with another string, and for repeating a string.

features.title: Object.assign()
features.summary: Copies own enumerable properties from one or more objects onto a target object.

migration.note: Object.assign also copies symbol-keyed properties and runs setters on the target.

features.title: Array.prototype.includes()
features.summary: Tests whether an array contains a value.

migration.note: includes can find NaN; indexOf cannot.

features.title: Exponentiation operator
features.summary: The ** operator and the **= assignment operator.

migration.note: ** is right-associative: 2 ** 3 ** 2 is 2 ** 9.

features.title: async functions and await
features.summary: async functions return promises, and await pauses them until a promise settles.

migration.note: An async function always returns a promise, even when it returns a plain value.

features.title: Object.values() and Object.entries()
features.summary: Return an object's own enumerable property values, or its key-value pairs.

features.title: Object rest and spread
features.summary: Rest and spread syntax for object properties: { ...a, ...b } and const { x, ...rest } = obj.

migration.note: Spread defines properties on the new object; Object.assign calls setters on its target.

features.title: Array.prototype.flat() and flatMap()
features.summary: Flatten nested arrays, or map and flatten in one step.

migration.note: flat() flattens one level by default; pass Infinity to flatten completely.

features.title: Optional catch binding
features.summary: A catch clause can omit the error variable when it is not needed.

features.title: Optional chaining
features.summary: The ?. operator stops and returns undefined when the left side is null or undefined.

migration.note: && stops on any falsy value (0, empty string, false). ?. stops only on null and undefined.

features.title: Nullish coalescing
features.summary: The ?? operator returns its right side only when the left side is null or undefined.

migration.note: || also replaces 0, empty strings and false. ?? replaces only null and undefined.

features.title: BigInt
features.summary: Integers of arbitrary size, written with an n suffix such as 123n.

features.title: Dynamic import()
features.summary: import() loads a module at run time and returns a promise for its namespace.

features.title: Logical assignment operators
features.summary: The &&=, ||= and ??= operators assign only when a condition on the left side holds.

migration.note: ||= replaces any falsy value. Use ??= to replace only null or undefined.

features.title: String.prototype.replaceAll()
features.summary: Replaces every occurrence of a string or pattern.

migration.note: A string argument is matched literally. A regular expression argument must have the g flag.

features.title: Class fields and private members
features.summary: Field declarations in class bodies, including #private fields and methods, static fields and static blocks.

migration.note: A #private field is enforced by the language. An _underscore name is only a convention.

features.title: Top-level await
features.summary: await can be used at the top level of a module.

migration.note: Only valid in module code.

features.title: Array.prototype.at()
features.summary: Reads an element by index, counting from the end when the index is negative. Also on strings and typed arrays.

features.title: Object.hasOwn()
features.summary: Tests whether an object has an own property, without going through the prototype.

features.title: findLast() and findLastIndex()
features.summary: Search an array from the end.

features.title: toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced() and with()
features.summary: Copying versions of sort, reverse and splice, plus with() to replace one element.

migration.note: sort(), reverse() and splice() change the array in place. The new methods return a copy.

features.title: Object.groupBy() and Map.groupBy()
features.summary: Group the items of an iterable by a key function.

migration.note: Object.groupBy returns an object with a null prototype.

features.title: Promise.withResolvers()
features.summary: Returns a promise together with its resolve and reject functions.

features.title: Iterator helpers
features.summary: Iterator methods such as map, filter, take, drop, flatMap and toArray, which work lazily.

migration.note: Helpers pull values one at a time. Spreading into an array first evaluates the whole sequence.

features.title: Set methods
features.summary: union(), intersection(), difference(), symmetricDifference(), isSubsetOf(), isSupersetOf() and isDisjointFrom().

features.title: Promise.try()
features.summary: Calls a function and always returns a promise, even if the function throws synchronously.

migration.note: A synchronous exception becomes a rejection.

features.title: Import attributes and JSON modules
features.summary: A with { type: "json" } clause on imports, used to import JSON modules.

features.title: Array.fromAsync()
features.summary: Builds an array from an async iterable and returns a promise for it.

features.title: Error.isError()
features.summary: Reliably tests whether a value is an error object.

migration.note: instanceof fails for errors created in another realm, such as an iframe.

features.title: using declarations
features.summary: using and await using declarations dispose of a resource automatically when the block ends.

migration.note: The resource needs a [Symbol.dispose]() method.

features.title: Temporal
features.summary: A modern date and time API that fixes many problems of the Date object.

features.title: Iterators and generators
features.summary: The iterator protocol, for...of loops, and generator functions (function*) that produce values with yield.

migration.note: A generator function returns an iterator that works with for...of and spread.

features.title: Map, Set, WeakMap and WeakSet
features.summary: Keyed and unique-value collections whose keys can be any value, not just strings.

migration.modern:
const counts = new Map();
words.forEach((word) => counts.set(word, (counts.get(word) || 0) + 1));
migration.note: A plain object only has string and symbol keys, and inherits properties such as toString.

features.title: Symbols
features.summary: A primitive type for unique property keys, including well-known symbols such as Symbol.iterator.

features.title: Proxy and Reflect
features.summary: Proxy objects intercept operations on another object, and Reflect exposes those operations as functions.

features.title: Typed arrays
features.summary: Fixed-type views over binary data, such as Uint8Array and Float64Array.

features.title: Array.from(), Array.of(), find() and friends
features.summary: Array.from, Array.of, find, findIndex, fill, copyWithin and the keys, values and entries iterators.

migration.note: Array.from also accepts any iterable and an optional mapping function.

features.title: Shorthand and computed object properties
features.summary: { name, age } shorthand, method shorthand, and [expression] computed property names in object literals.

migration.legacy:
var user = { name: name, age: age };
user[prefix + "Id"] = id;

features.title: Number and Math additions
features.summary: Number.isInteger, Number.isSafeInteger, Number.EPSILON, Math.trunc, Math.sign, Math.hypot and related functions.

migration.legacy: var isInt = typeof x === "number" && isFinite(x) && Math.floor(x) === x;
migration.note: Number.isNaN and Number.isFinite do not convert their argument, unlike the global isNaN and isFinite.

features.title: Unicode code point support
features.summary: String.fromCodePoint(), codePointAt(), normalize(), \u{...} escapes and the u flag for regular expressions.

features.title: padStart() and padEnd()
features.summary: Pad a string to a minimum length at the start or the end.

features.title: Trailing commas in parameters
features.summary: A trailing comma is allowed in function parameter lists and call arguments.

migration.note: Adding a parameter later changes only one line in a diff.

features.title: SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics
features.summary: Memory shared between agents and atomic operations for coordinating access to it.

features.title: Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors()
features.summary: Returns the full property descriptors of an object, including getters and setters.

features.title: Async iteration and async generators
features.summary: for await...of loops and async function* generators for sequences that arrive over time.

migration.note: The source must be an async iterable, meaning it has a Symbol.asyncIterator method.

features.title: Promise.prototype.finally()
features.summary: Runs a callback when a promise settles, whether it was fulfilled or rejected.

migration.note: The callback receives no arguments, and the original result or error passes through.

features.title: Named capture groups
features.summary: (?<name>...) captures that can be read from the groups property of a match.

features.title: Lookbehind assertions
features.summary: (?<=...) and (?<!...) match text only when it is preceded, or not preceded, by a pattern.

migration.legacy:
var match = /\$(\d+)/.exec(text);
var amount = match && match[1];
migration.modern:
var match = /(?<=\$)\d+/.exec(text);
var amount = match && match[0];
migration.note: The lookbehind is checked but not included in the match.

features.title: Unicode property escapes
features.summary: \p{...} and \P{...} match characters by Unicode property, with the u flag.

migration.note: The older pattern only covers ASCII letters.

features.title: The s (dotAll) flag
features.summary: With the s flag, . also matches line terminators.

features.title: Object.fromEntries()
features.summary: Builds an object from key-value pairs. It is the inverse of Object.entries().

features.title: trimStart() and trimEnd()
features.summary: Standard names for trimming one side of a string. They replace the older trimLeft() and trimRight().

migration.note: trimLeft and trimRight are still available as aliases in Annex B.

features.title: Array.prototype.sort()
features.summary: Sorts an array in place. The default order compares elements as strings.

history.note: sort must be stable: elements that compare as equal keep their original relative order.
The algorithm is specified more precisely, so fewer cases leave the result order up to the implementation.

features.title: Function.prototype.toString()
features.summary: Returns a string describing a function.
